title: LK Advani, 98, Admitted to Delhi Hospital With Chest Infection, Condition Stable
excerpt: The former deputy prime minister was brought to Indraprastha Apollo Hospital on Friday evening and is under observation in the pulmonary department. It is his third hospital admission in under two years.
body:
• LK Advani, 98, was admitted to Indraprastha Apollo Hospital in Delhi on Friday evening, around 7:30 p.m., with a chest infection.
  • He is in the pulmonary department, under observation by a team of doctors, and his condition is stable, hospital officials said.
  • This is his third hospital stay in under two years: he was admitted in May this year for age-related complications and spent time in intensive care in December 2024.
  • Advani, a former deputy prime minister and one of the BJP's founding figures, turns 99 on November 8. He received the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honour, in 2024.

Veteran Bharatiya Janata Party leader Lal Krishna Advani was admitted to Indraprastha Apollo Hospital in Delhi on Friday evening with a chest infection. The 98-year-old former deputy prime minister was brought to the hospital at around 7:30 p.m. and admitted to the pulmonary department, where a team of doctors is monitoring him, according to reports by NDTV, Mint and the IANS news agency. His condition is stable, hospital officials said, and medical tests are underway.

A recurring pattern of hospital stays

This is not Advani's first admission in recent months. He was last admitted to the same hospital in May this year with age-related health complications and was discharged after a few days under medical care. Earlier, in December 2024, he was treated in the hospital's intensive care unit for medical management and investigations under the supervision of a neurologist; the hospital reported gradual improvement at the time and said he was likely to be moved out of intensive care within days.

https://x.com/IndiaToday/status/2111152671713558893

At 98, any chest infection is treated seriously, and pulmonary infections are among the most common reasons elderly patients require hospital observation. The hospital has not announced a discharge date, and no party statement beyond the confirmation of his stable condition had been issued as of Saturday morning.

The man who built the modern BJP

Advani is one of the most consequential figures in the BJP's history. He served three terms as party president — from 1986 to 1990, 1993 to 1998, and 2004 to 2005 — and his 1990 Ram Rath Yatra is widely credited with transforming the party from a marginal force into a national contender. In the National Democratic Alliance government led by Atal Bihari Vajpayee, he served as Union home minister from 1998 to 2004 and as deputy prime minister from 2002 to 2004.

Born on November 8, 1927, in Karachi, in what was then undivided India, Advani moved to India after Partition and rose through the Bharatiya Jana Sangh, the BJP's predecessor, before becoming one of the new party's founding leaders in 1980. Prime Minister Narendra Modi greeted him on his birthday last year as a statesman with a towering vision. In 2024 he was awarded the Bharat Ratna, India's highest civilian honour, following the Padma Vibhushan in 2015.

What happens next

Advani remains under observation while tests are completed. He turns 99 on November 8, three weeks from now. Further medical bulletins from the hospital will determine whether this admission follows the pattern of his May stay — a few days of treatment followed by discharge — and party leaders are expected to visit or issue statements as updates emerge.
